title: Netherlands – Polythene waste and refuse sacks and bags – PMD- en luierzakken 2027 ev voor 12 gemeenten
description: Bizob besteedt aan namens de gemeenten Bergeijk, Bladel, Cranendonck, Eersel, Maashorst, Meierijstad, Oirschot, Reusel-de Mierden, Veldhoven, Vught en werkorganisatie MijnGemeenteDichtbij. De overeenkomst bestaat uit de levering van inzamelzakken van 100% gerecycled LDPE voor: Plastic, Metaal, Drankenkartons (PMD) / Plastic, Blik en Drinkkarton (PBD). In het aanbestedingsdocument spreken we overwegend van PMD. Luiers en incontinentiemateriaal, in het aanbestedingsdocument aangeduid als: luierzak-ken. De opdracht betreft een samengevoegde opdracht, in zowel geografisch opzicht (clustering van gemeenten) als op productniveau (PMD-inzamelzakken en luierzakken). Het samenvoegen in geografisch opzicht zorgt voor een zo groot mogelijk volume van het in grote mate gestandaardiseerd product. Een groot volume heeft een positieve invloed op de prijs. Daarnaast kan er door de gezamenlijke aanpak centraal contractmanagement worden uitgevoerd. Door het samenvoegen is de opdracht voor meerdere partijen interessant en de afleverafstanden zijn beperkt, omdat bestellingen gecombineerd uitgeleverd kunnen worden. In deze markt zijn hoofdzakelijk grote spelers werkzaam. Om de opdracht ook toegankelijk te maken voor het MKB is deze verdeeld in percelen. De opdracht wordt onderverdeeld in de volgende percelen: - Perceel 1: PMD-zakken (geel) - Perceel 2: Luierzakken - Perceel 3: PBD-zakken (oranje) Per perceel wordt er per gemeente met één opdrachtnemer een overeenkomst aangegaan. De overeenkomst wordt aangegaan voor een periode van minimaal twee jaar en maximaal zes jaar. De ingangsdatum van de overeenkomsten is: 1 maart 2027

title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. title: USS WICHITA (LCS 13) Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) - Paint OEM and Technical Services
description: This solicitation is for commercial items and has been prepared in accordance with the format outlined in FAR Subpart 12.6, supplemented with additional information contained in this notice. This announcement constitutes the sole solicitation; quotes are hereby requested. Request for Proposal (RFP) No. N40027-26-R-0008 is issues as a FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION solicitation and is being processed under FAR Part 13 � Simplified Acquisition Procedures and FAR Part 6- Competition Requirements. The applicable North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code is 325510 � Paint and Coating Manufacturing. Scope of Requirements The Government seeks sources that can provide support as follows: Product Provision: Provide paint, coatings, and preservation products per the Government's Work Statement. Navy Paint Warranty: Paint, coatings, and preservation products must meet the required standards per the attached Navy Paint Warranty (Attachment 3). No Waivers/Subcontracts: The responding vendor must provide the required warranty directly, without waiver or subcontracting. OEM Certification: Offerors must provide proof of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) certification for the paint and coating systems. Qualified Personnel: Provide Field Service Technical Representatives (FSTR) that meet or exceed the minimum qualifications within the Work Statement in order to perform, inspect, and certify the work stated. Personnel may not be substituted without express written approval by the Government. Hull Coating System: Provide a twelve (12) year antifouling, underwater hull, and boot top coating system that complies with epoxy anticorrosive MIL-PRF-24647, Type I or II, and that complies with antifouling paint MIL-PRF-24647, Type II. Marking Compatibility: Provide preservation products that are suitable for use as hull and boot top markings on the ablative antifoulant paints. Substrate Compatibility: All preservation products must be compatible and have the ability to be applied over any existing coating on like surfaces. Statutory and Licensing Requirements Homeport Statute (10 U.S.C. 7299A): In accordance with the "Homeport Statute", this procurement will solicit offers only from offerors capable of performing the work in the Mayport homeport area. Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR): Offerors must have, or be able to obtain, an Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR) or Government-approved equivalency by the time of contract award. Anticipated Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price (FFP). Evaluation Method: Price-Only (Among conforming, responsible, and technically acceptable offerors�not a structured Part 15 LPTA). II. Summary of Navy Paint Warranty (Attachment 3) The successful contractor will be required to provide an express Marine Coatings Warranty (incorporated into FAR 52.212-4(o) Addendum) that includes: Two-Year Application Durability: Warranting that the paint is applied correctly so that it lasts a minimum of two (2) years after the date of application, and that the paint is usable up to its expiration date. Premature Failure Remedies: In the event of premature failure (e.g., delaminating, blistering, rust-through, softening, peeling), the Contractor shall furnish, at no cost to the Government, all materials and technical representative services necessary to recoat the failed area at any domestic or foreign location designated by the Government. Hull Scamping: Providing scamping of the underwater hull at no cost to the Government if more than twenty (20) percent of the underwater hull is heavily fouled due to poor performance of the antifouling within two (2) years of application. Misapplication Notice: The warranty is not voided by shipyard misapplication unless the Contractor's technical representative provides timely notice (written within 24 hours of verbal notice, and no later than 8 hours after the event) specifying the affected areas and required remedial actions. III. Questions for Industry The notice of interest should include a brief description of your company, its capabilities as they relate to the requirements, and answers to the following specific questions. Please limit your response to no more than five (5) pages (excluding certifications or licenses). Is your company a small or large business as defined by the Small Business Administration (SBA) under NAICS code 325510 (Paint and Coating Manufacturing)? If a small business, please specify your socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), Women-Owned (WOSB), HUBZone, Veteran-Owned (VOSB), or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVOSB)). How many employees does your company have? Does your company have an active website? If so, what is your company's website address? Does your company have a satisfactory performance record for this type of marine preservation work? Please provide examples of relevant and recent (within the last three years) past performance. Is your company able to provide both the desired paint product AND the manufacturer's guarantee/warranty without waiver or subcontracting, as detailed in the "Scope of Requirements" and "Navy Paint Warranty"? Given the complexity of the work described in this announcement, please describe your company's historical experience completing services on similar ship classes (e.g., Littoral Combat Ships or similar naval vessels) or briefly describe how your company is capable of meeting these requirements by the time of contract award. Given the complexity and size of the work described, does your company plan to submit a proposal/quote in response to the anticipated solicitation for the paint coatings and technical services of USS THE WICHITA (LCS 13)? IV. Submission Instructions Information provided shall be treated as Business Sensitive or Confidential to the responder, exempt from public release under the Freedom of Information Act. All information shall be provided free of charge to the Government. SERMC may request further information regarding the capabilities of respondents to meet the requirements set forth in the announcement. Where and When to Submit All proposals must be submitted electronically via email with the subject line: "USS WICHITA (LCS 13) Docked Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) - Paint OEM N4002726R0008". title: Army CONUS Enterprise (ACE) Land Mobile Radio (LMR) � Motorola OEM Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support for Fort Novosel, AL and Holston Army Ammunition Plant (HAAP), TN
description: NOTICE OF INTENT-SOURCES SOUGHT The Defense Information Systems Agency /Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc. A sole source Justification & Approval document is being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted to SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301. The proposed contract action is for Army CONUS Enterprise (ACE) Land Mobile Radio (LMR) - Motorola Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support for Fort Novosel, Alabama, and Holston Army Ammunition Plant (HAAP), Tennessee. The period of performance is September 30, 2026, September 29, 2027, with one, one year option period. The requirement provides continued OEM extended warranty and associated maintenance support for Government-accepted Motorola LMR equipment and components covered by the applicable OEM warranty entitlement. Support includes OEM warranty administration; OEM technical support; diagnosis of covered equipment failures; repair or replacement of covered components; Return Material Authorization processing; warranty-related software and firmware updates made available under OEM entitlement; replacement components required to fulfill warranty obligations; applicable licensing; transportation and shipping associated with warranty actions; and coordination and tracking of warranty actions through closure. The contractor is required to provide OEM-backed technical and lifecycle support to ensure the continued operation of the existing Motorola LMR systems and maintain warranty coverage throughout the period of performance. At this time, the incumbent contractor Motorola Solutions, Inc.(Motorola) is the only source capable of fulfilling the requirement for OEM extended warranty and maintenance support for the existing Motorola LMR systems and associated equipment. As the OEM, Motorola, possesses the proprietary technical data, system-specific knowledge, OEM repair capabilities, software and firmware support, replacement components, licensing, and warranty authority necessary to provide continued OEM-backed coverage for the installed Motorola equipment. Awarding this requirement to another source would not provide the required Motorola OEM extended warranty coverage and could jeopardize the Government�s ability to maintain OEM-supported maintenance, compatibility, and lifecycle support for the existing Motorola LMR infrastructure and equipment. Such an outcome would introduce significant risks to mission-critical communications, operational readiness, and the security of Army Enterprise LMR systems. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 USC 2304 (c) (1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 15 days of this notification and include a detailed capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a request for proposal. A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source nature of the requirement. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 334210, Telephone Apparatus Manufacturing, will be used for determining company size status. CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The Motorola OEM Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support requirement is currently being performed under the following contract: Contract Number: HC108424P0005 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Incumbent and Size: Motorola Solutions, Inc. � Large Business CAGE: 78205 Method of Previous Acquisition: Sole Source Period of Performance: July 31, 2024 through September 30, 2026 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall be the OEM, Motorola Solutions, Inc., or possess the necessary OEM authorization and capabilities to provide the required Motorola OEM extended warranty and maintenance support for the covered LMR systems and associated equipment in accordance with the PWS. Points of Contact: Contracting Officer: Melyssa D. Lafontaine, melyssa.d.lafontaine.civ@mail.mil Contract Specialist: Bobby J. Drees-Douglas, bobby.j.drees-douglas.civ@mail.mil

title: USCGC Stratton Shaft Alignment and Bearing Reaction Check
description: Statement of Work CGC Stratton Shaft Alignment and Bearing Reaction Check Intent: contractor must measure and report to USCG the Vertical and Horizontal Loads on the (2) bull gear bearings and (2) intermediate bearings, stern and strut bearings, using the Strain Gage Method. Period of Performance: 01 November 2026 � 01 January 2027 Location: USCGC Stratton, 42 Eagle Road Coast Guard Island, Alameda CA 94501 Contractor will install a total of (5) full bridge strain gage sets on the Port shaft, and (5) strain gage sets on the Starboard shaft, to complete the bearing load calculations. Contractor will also measure and report the vertical load on each line shaft bearing using the Hydraulic Jack/Load Cell method. Contractor will provide all specialty tools and calibrated instrumentation necessary to install the strain gages and measure the strain gage data. Contractor shall provide a final written report within 15 days after completion of the work covered by this scope of work. The report shall contain at a minimum the following: Introduction and References Project description Alignment calculations Alignment tests with strain gages Conclusions Recommendation for future action Data sheets on shaft model used to obtain reported results e.g. stations, strain gauge locations, diameters, lengths, load points, etc. Data sheets from Computer runs that computed reported results e.g. stations, deflections, stresses, bearing reactions, slopes, etc. References: Coast Guard Drawings Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 114-001, Rev B, Fairwaters and Rope Guard Installation Details & L/M (ASC114001) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 243-007, Rev E, Propulsion Shafting System Arrangement (ASC243008) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 243-008, Rev -, Propulsion Shafting and Appendage (ASC243001B) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 244-001, Rev -, Propulsion Shafting System Measured Bearing Reaction Report (ASC244001) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 244-002, Rev B, Stern Tube Seal & Strut Bearings Arrangement & Details & L/M (ASC244002) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 244-003, Rev -, Propulsion Shafting System Measured Bearing Reaction Report (AS2244001 Notes: For any references to be distributed, the contractor must be registered in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) through Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) and provide your JCP number to the listed point of contact for this work. For questions regarding this statement of work, contact LTJG Maximos Brady maximos.h.brady@uscg.mil

title: Guatemala – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Asistencia Técnica para la implementación de la Agenda de inversiones Global Gateway en Guatemala – Global Gateway Facility Guatemala
description: En 2021, la Comisión Europea lanzó la estrategia de inversiones Global Gateway, que tiene como objetivo fomentar inversiones de gran calibre en infraestructura verde y digital en los países socios, con soluciones innovadoras y de calidad, creando al mismo tiempo valor añadido local y promoviendo el crecimiento económico, el empleo y la cohesión social. Durante la III Cumbre UE-CELAC, celebrada en julio de 2023, los dirigentes de ambas regiones reafirmaron su compromiso de reforzar la asociación birregional, reconociendo la importancia de la Agenda de Inversiones Global Gateway. Dicho compromiso fue renovado durante la IV Cumbre UE-CELAC celebrada en noviembre de 2025. El objetivo general de esta acción es contribuir a la implementación de inversiones sostenibles y transformadoras en los sectores de transición verde y digital en Guatemala, donde haya un interés común europeo y de la agenda de desarrollo de Guatemala, y ello en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway, asegurando su alineación con las prioridades estratégicas del país y fomentando un desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible. La Asistencia Técnica contribuirá a: mejorar la alineación, coordinación y monitoreo de las iniciativas implementadas en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway en Guatemala; promover un marco regulatorio e institucional que favorezca la inversión sostenible en los sectores prioritarios de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway; impulsar proyectos de inversión sostenibles, transformadores y sensibles a la igualdad de género y a las buenas prácticas internacionales en materia de derechos y protección del medioambiente en los sectores prioritarios y a posicionar los intereses del sector privado europeo en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway para Guatemala. Sin excluir otras potenciales áreas de trabajo prioritarias para la UE y Guatemala, y reconociendo la flexibilidad dinámica de la estrategia Global Gateway, las áreas prioritarias para Guatemala actualmente incluyen transición verde (transporte sostenible, energía renovable e integración eléctrica regional, economía circular, gestión sostenible de recursos naturales y residuos) y transición digital (conectividad, gobernanza digital, ciberseguridad, innovación digital, observación de la Tierra, inteligencia artificial).

title: Ireland – Construction work – RFT 02/26/GM - Works Contractor and PSCS for ATU Dublin Road EEDPP2 Energy Retrofit at Atlantic Technological University at the Galway City Campus
description: Atlantic Technological University (ATU) is seeking suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake an energy retrofit project at its Galway City Dublin Road Campus. The project comprises the retrofit of approximately 4,425m² of the original 1972 building and forms part of the Higher Education Authority (HEA) and Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI) funded Energy Efficiency and Decarbonisation Pathfinder Project (EEDPP2). The works include building fabric upgrades, roof and window replacement, ventilation improvements, lighting and controls upgrades, and the installation of a medium-temperature air-source heat pump, with existing gas boilers retained for peak demand and backup. The project aims to improve energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, extend the building's operational life, enhance occupant comfort, increase the use of renewable technologies, and achieve a minimum B1 BER rating. The existing building is a reinforced concrete framed structure currently served by the campus central heating system and a combination of natural and mechanical ventilation systems.

title: Technical Assistance to Embed Renewable Integration in Madagascar Mining Permits
description: La description de l'appel d'offres ainsi que les documents de soumission sont également disponibles en français. Veuillez consulter les pièces jointes pour plus d'informations. Following the reopening of mining permits in 2026, Madagascar has an opportunity to shape how new mining investments source power. While mining and environmental regulations are in place, renewable energy integration is not yet embedded within licensing and permitting requirements. The assignment will support the Government of Madagascar to design, adopt and implement a Green Mining Energy Framework that embeds renewable energy requirements into mining licensing, environmental permitting and ESIA processes. Key outputs include a diagnostic and design options package, a Green Mining Energy Framework and supporting guidance for government adoption, and an implementation and compliance package with templates, monitoring tools and capacity-building support. The project aims to reduce future diesel dependence in the mining sector and support lower-emission mining development in Madagascar. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

title: Unlocking Commercial and Industrial Captive Renewable Energy in Uganda: Market Sizing and Regulatory Reform
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to Uganda's Electricity Regulatory Authority (ERA). Uganda's electricity sector is predominantly powered by renewable energy and demand is growing rapidly. However, uptake of commercial and industrial (C&I) captive renewable energy remains limited due to regulatory gaps, insufficient market data, and barriers to investment. This is particularly significant given the growing role of behind-the-meter renewable energy as a means of reducing diesel reliance, improving energy security, and supporting economic growth. The assignment will support ERA, in partnership with the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD) and electricity distributors UEDCL, WENRECO and KIS, to strengthen the enabling environment for C&I captive renewable energy. The work will establish an evidence base on market demand, existing captive generation and grid capacity, review Uganda's regulatory framework and international best practice, and develop targeted regulatory and market-enabling solutions. Key outputs are expected to include recommendations for a mid-tier regulatory framework, updated settlement and implementation guidance, standardised commercial documentation, and financing pathways to improve project bankability. The project aims to increase private-sector investment in captive renewable energy, accelerate deployment, reduce dependence on diesel generation, and strengthen Uganda's energy security and grid resilience. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

description: This service is for the procurement, installation, configuration, and commissioning of a modern electronic smart key box system to support secure, auditable management of physical brass keys used by the Security Services Office (SSO), the Security Operations Center (SOC), and other authorized CDC personnel. Many CDC facilities utilize brass keys either as the primary means of access (for non?PACS?controlled spaces) or as a redundant fallback method when PACS doors are unavailable due to power, controller, network, or hardware failure. Improving the 3 accountability and security of these keys is critical to protecting CDC assets, staff, and facilities. The purpose of this requirement is to strengthen the physical security posture of CDC facilities by deploying an enterprise class smart key management platform that: � Improves accountability and traceability of key issuance and return. � Reduces risk associated with loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to controlled keys. � Provides SOC with real?time visibility into key access events. � Supports PIV credentials and MFA methods, including PIN and/or biometrics. � Integrates seamlessly with CDC networks, SOC consoles, and SSO workflows. � Ensures operational continuity through backup power and controlled manual override capabilities. � Supports overall OSSAM/SSO mission readiness in alignment with CDC security policies. These systems will be installed and integrated at the following locations: � Roybal Campus, Building 20 (SOC) � 80-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 17 � 40-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 18 � 40-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 23 � 40-key capacity. � Chamblee Campus, Building 106 � 40-key capacity. � Lawrenceville Campus � 20-key capacity.This project will modernize the outdated systems and processes CDC�s asset key control. The SOC manages access to all high value and restricted spaces mostly but also to regular calls for service of lockouts. The current key box is outdate and often fails through long down periods. Specialist are using manual and outdated procedures to issue key defeating the original intent of an electronic key control box. The number and placement of the boxes also reduces the risk of losing a key as well as traversing campuses across the metro Atlanta area.

title: NOTICE OF INTENT (NOI) TO SOLE SOURCE - UPS Battery Replacement
description: The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) requires a professional, full-string battery replacement service for one (1) Liebert NX 80-120 Uninterruptible Power System (UPS) and its associated forty (40) Enersys HX505 Valve-Regulated Lead-Acid (VRLA) sealed batteries (jars). The Contractor shall provide all labor, transportation, tools, calibrated equipment, materials, and supervision necessary to safely perform a complete, full-string VRLA battery replacement for forty (40) Enersys HX505 sealed batteries (or OEM-approved equivalent) connected to the Vertiv Liebert NX 80-120 UPS system. This procurement falls under NAICS code 335999 � Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors, which has a size standard of 600 employees. This action is processed under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (RFO) Part 12. Market research indicates that competition is not feasible for the following reasons: Vertiv corporation is the manufacturer of the Liebert NX 80-120 Uninterruptible Power System (UPS) which uses the Vertiv VRLA Batteries as its backup power supply. These batteries are at the end of life and requires replacement. Vertiv is the only vendor capable of providing the battery and installation service without requiring a costly and highly disruptive physical installation from a competitor. Transitioning to a new provider would force the government to fund redundant infrastructure, undergo lengthy equipment replacements, and face significant service delays. Awarding this contract to Vertiv leverages their pre-existing network footprint, proven compliance with JBSA security protocols, and established base relationships, ensuring immediate operational readiness at a fair and accurate price point. This informational notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, interested parties capable of fulfilling this requirement may submit a capability statement by the published deadline. Submissions must provide clear and convincing evidence that competing this action is advantageous to the Government. The Government retains sole discretion to determine whether to compete this procurement based on the responses received. The response period is abbreviated due to the urgency of the requirement.

title: Army Blood Link (ABL) � Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS)
description: Army Blood Link (ABL) � Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) for Blood Product Transport Request for Proposals (RFP) � Other Transaction Authority (OTA) Prototype Project Brief Description of Requirement The 419th Contracting Support Brigade, Fort Liberty, North Carolina, on behalf of XVIII Airborne Corps Joint Operations Innovation Outpost (JIOP), is issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) for the competitive award of an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) prototype project for the Army Blood Link (ABL) Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS). The Government seeks to develop and deliver two (2) prototype UAS capable of transporting 20 units of Government?designated blood products per mission, including all approved primary, secondary, thermal?control, shock?protection, monitoring, and restraint packaging. Each system shall provide a minimum usable payload?compartment volume of 1.25 cubic feet and a minimum payload capacity of 35 pounds, with a payload capacity range of 25�50 pounds. The contractor shall provide a validated transport container that maintains the Government?specified product temperature range for the required mission duration and environmental conditions. The ABL UAS will be employed in contested and denied environments where ground transportation is not viable and will support both training and deployed operational missions for medical units (e.g., medical brigades). Additional technical, performance, and interface requirements are provided in the attached Salient Characteristics � Army Blood Link (ABL) UAS for Blood Product Transport, which form an integral part of this notice and the basis for proposal evaluation. Period and Place of Performance a. Prototype Period of Performance (PoP): The anticipated PoP for the prototype OTA is up to 3 months from effective date of award, unless otherwise negotiated. (Recommend modification of existing commercial UAS) Offerors shall propose a schedule that delivers fully functional prototype systems (including complete payload containers and support equipment) no later than 3 months after award, including time allocated to testing, refinement, and documentation in coordination with the Government. b. Place of Performance / Delivery Location: Primary delivery and demonstration locations will be within the continental United States (CONUS). The initial delivery location is anticipated to be: Fort Liberty, North Carolina (or other designated XVIII Airborne Corps / medical unit location). Specific delivery instructions, test locations, and access requirements will be provided at time of award and coordinated with the Agreements Officer�s Representative (AOR). Anticipated Agreement Information a. Type of Instrument: This effort will be executed as a prototype project agreement under DoD Other Transaction Authority (OTA). b. Type of Contract/Agreement Consideration: The ABL prototype effort will be structured as a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) OTA agreement for the design, integration, delivery, and demonstration of the prototype systems, in accordance with the DoD OTA Guide and applicable implementing guidance. c. Acquisition Procedures: Acquisition procedures will follow OTA prototype project procedures as outlined in the DoD OTA Guide and implementing Army guidance for competitive prototype projects. d. Authority: This prototype project is pursued under Title 10, U.S.C., Section 4022 (Other Transaction Authority for Prototype Projects). e. Follow?On Production: This competitive prototype project may result in a follow?on production agreement (which may be FFP or other appropriate structure) without the use of competitive procedures, consistent with Title 10, U.S.C., Section 4022. Follow?on production is contingent upon: Successful completion of the prototype effort, as determined by the AOR; and Increased or continued demand for the ABL capability; and A clear Government determination that a follow?on production award is in the best interest of the Government. Summary of Technical and Operational Requirements The ABL UAS shall meet or exceed the requirements set forth in the attached Salient Characteristics document, including but not limited to: Mission Role & Employment: Transport Government?designated blood products in contested/denied environments where ground transportation is not viable. Support training missions (1�5 per month) and operational deployments (multiple missions per day). Payload Capacity & Volume: Transport 20 blood units including all packaging and protection. Minimum usable payload volume 1.25 ft�. Payload capacity range 25�50 lb, with minimum 35 lb capability. Blood Transport Container & Thermal Control: Validated container compatible with UAS payload bay. Maintain required blood temperature for up to 3 hours at 15 �F to 120 �F with high humidity. Protection against rain, dust, sand, solar heating, and chemical contamination. Range, Endurance & Mission Distance: Minimum 30 km one?way operational radius at maximum combined fuel/energy and payload load. 100 km maximum mission distance (total route). 3�6 hours of operating time per mission, while ensuring blood remains within specified temperature limits (? 3 hours in container). Operations & Environment: Day and night operations. Operation from ground level to 18,000 ft. Operate at 15 �F to 120 �F, high humidity. Delivery & Accuracy: Delivery?location accuracy of ? 10 meters. Support ground/landing delivery and optional aerial drop from 10�15 m without compromising blood integrity. Command, Control & Communications: Minimum 30?mile communications range between aircraft and ground control station. Single?operator control of at least one aircraft, with architecture that allows multiple aircraft to operate simultaneously in the same area. Autonomy & Detect?and?Avoid: Semi?autonomous flight, waypoint navigation, and return?to?base. Sensors and logic to detect and avoid aircraft and obstacles, suitable for contested/denied environments. Training & Human Factors: Operator training program (approximately 1�3 days) for basic operations, servicing, and field?level repair. System suitable for operation and servicing by typical medical brigade personnel with minimal technical background. Maintainability, Reliability & Service Life: Expected operational life 500�1500 flight hours. Servicing intervals every 300�500 cycles. Field?repairable by unit personnel with modular/line?replaceable components. Minimum 90% probability of successful delivery per mission. At least one?year warranty and obsolescence/parts?availability plan. Regulatory, Origin & Approval Requirements: Design and documentation sufficient to support U.S. Army Systems Readiness Directorate (SRD) flight approval. No prohibited foreign?made components, foreign software, foreign cloud services, or foreign technical support. Compliance with applicable U.S. and DoD sourcing restrictions. Meeting these salient characteristics within a 20% deviation from the stated parameters is acceptable; however, proposals will be evaluated competitively and only one awardee is anticipated. Evaluation Factors All proposals will be evaluated in accordance with the Competition Evaluation Factors for the Army Blood Link (ABL), attached to this notice. The following factors and relative weights (total = 1.0) will be used to rank proposals: Price � Weight: 0.30 Total proposed price and overall value relative to technical performance and schedule. Compact Design & Portability � Weight: 0.20 Compliance with packed size/weight constraints; ease of transport, setup, and loading by medical personnel; and compact integration of the payload container. Technical Performance & Mission Effectiveness � Weight: 0.15 Ability to meet or exceed key salient characteristics (payload, range, endurance, accuracy, environmental performance, day/night ops, comms range). Demonstrated mission effectiveness and proposed delivery schedule (prototype delivery within 3 months of award). Thermal Control & Payload Protection � Weight: 0.10 Performance

title: Z1DA--LOADING DOCK CONCRETE REPAIRS
description: DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS Network Contracting Office 6 (NCO 6) Sources Sought Notice: 36C24626Q1077 In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul Part 10.000 this Request for Information is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Quotation (RFQ), nor an offer to negotiate or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs. Responses are strictly voluntary. Respondents will not be compensated, and all information becomes property of the Government upon submission. Additionally, the Government reserves the right to revise and refine contract requirements before the release of any associated solicitation. 1. Title. Loading Dock Concrete Repair 2. Background. The Central Virginia VA Health Care System is requesting loading dock concrete repair at the Richmond VA Medical Center (VAMC). The loading dock treads and risers are damaged and is a safety concern. Period of Performance: project should take approximately 90 days to complete. 3. Scope. This statement of work outlines the labor, materials, safety requirements and construction processes required to repair the loading dock structure at the Richmond VA Medical Center. All work shall be performed in accordance with VA Design Guides, VA Master Specifications, OSHA 29 CFR 1926, and applicable state, federal, and local regulations. The contractor will repair the existing structure as well as the stairs treads and risers to the proper height as previous measurements. The contractor will also use rebar and steel dowls for added structure strength. The contractor will use 350 PSI concrete and install yellow safety treads on the existing stairs. The contractor will also seal the concrete to protect it from weather. The contractor will provide all labor, materials, tools, equipment, travel, qualified service technicians and supervision. 4. Specific Tasks. Key tasks include: Demolish existing failed concrete and damaged stair components Remove deteriorated #4 reinforcement steel Reconstruct loading dock platform and stair system to VA structural dimensions Install new structural reinforcement tied into existing concrete Place 3500 PSI concrete for the platform, stairs, and edge reconstruction Install VA-required safety bumpers and yellow tread markings Apply required finishing and concrete sealant Comply with all VA and OSHA safety protocols (including daily JHAs) BUSINESS TYPE AND SIZE: For market research purposes, all responses to this notice will be reviewed, regardless of small business/socioeconomic category, including those firms that are identified as large businesses. Review of responses to this notice will support later determination of set-aside requirements, if a solicitation becomes available, where the rule of two is met regarding a set-aside, including set-asides under 38 U.S.C. 8127 and 8128 for SDVOSB and/or VOSB firms registered in the SBA Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert) database, in accordance with priorities set by regulation. NOTE: A set-aside category has not been determined. The information compiled by this sources-sought will be used to make the determination on the best procurement strategy for this requirement based on the current market. ADMINISTRATIVE: The Department of Veterans Affairs anticipates awarding a one-time, Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Contract. FAR 36.204(b) Disclosure of the magnitude of Construction projects: Between $25,000 and $100,000. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this action being considered are 238110 with a size standard of $19 Million. However, the results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the final NAICS code and procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING: 1. Please provide a positive statement of interest in submitting a quote based on the general scope of work description. 2. Please identify your company s business and/or socioeconomic category. If your company is either Small, Large, Women owned, SDVOSB or VOSB, etc. Also state whether you are currently certified for North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) 238110 Poured Concrete Foundation and Structure Contractors. Current SBA size standard for NAICS 238110 is $19M. 3. Please provide a capability statement. Describe your company s in-house capability to accomplish the summarized project scope/goal; and confirm that your company can obtain performance and payment bonds to cover 100% of the value of the requirement. 4. The objective of this project is to provide a complete Design-Review, Engineering, Construction Documents, Construction, Testing, Commissioning, and Turnover solution for the construction of a new dormitory facility at the Instituto T�cnico Policial (ITP) in Comayagua, Honduras The Government�s Bridging Documents (See Appendix A) establish the proposed architectural layout, functional requirements, preliminary structural concept, and overall project configuration for the new EIC Training Facility. title: 7G21--Teleradiology Stations
description: Description Teleradiology stations which consist of a computer tower, large radiology specific double screen reading monitor (31.5"), plus side monitor (23.8" FHD IPS) and UPS units at each station to ensure surge protection. These are specifically built computers and monitors for radiologists to use in primary diagnostic interpretation all types of radiology exams, as well as viewing the patient electronic health record, and completion of other administrative tasks. Scope of Work Objective: Procure, configure, and deploy seven (7) radiology reading workstations with associated hardware, software, calibration, reading monitors, side monitors and UPS units, in alignment with VA radiology specific requirements and American College of Radiology (ACR) monitor requirements for primary diagnostic interpretation (including mammography). Vendor must have responsive and robust customer support in case of downtime emergency or as needed for trouble shooting. Each station will enable a radiologist to complete their work remotely off site. Being remote and more challenging to update/repair they need to match exactly our existing teleradiology stations so they can be swapped out with existing stations as needed for service.

description: COMBINED PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT (COMMERCIAL OFF-THE-SHELF EVERSOFT SOFTWARE) FAR Part 12 This special notice meets posting requirements of RFO FAR 5.1, 6.1, 12.1 and DFARS 206.3. It also serves as market research pursuant to RFO FAR 10. The Government intends to award a 5-year, sole-source, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)/Enterprise Contract (EC) with the first order to be issued prior to the conclusion of Fiscal Year 2026. Anticipated Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Intended Sole Source OEM: Everfox (https://www.everfox.com/) Estimated Contract Ceiling: $75M-$90M This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIRED SUPPLIES AND SERVICES The Government has an ongoing operational requirement to procure enterprise-level, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software licenses, specialized hardware appliances, hardware/software maintenance, and engineering support services provided by Everfox. (or brand-name equivalent solutions satisfying all salient characteristics) The requirement encompasses a 5-year Ordering Period. Specific part numbers, nomenclature, and projected annual quantities across the total ordering period are itemized in the attached spreadsheet ("Attachment 1 - Requirements Listing"). The required supplies and services are categorized across three core areas: A. SOFTWARE LICENSES, SUBSCRIPTIONS, AND MAINTENANCE Cross-Domain Guards: Perpetual and subscription licenses, standard maintenance, and associated filter bundles for Structured Guard (2070 Series), Unstructured Guard (2068 Series), and High-Speed Guard (2071 Series) supporting multi-network data transfer. Centralized Management & Endpoint Access: Control Center Server and Managed Device subscriptions (CCMDS/CCSVS Series) and Trusted Thin Client (TTC) Distribution Console, End User Device (EUD), and Network Resource licenses (10251 Series). Collaboration & Security Plugins: Everfox Information eXchange (DSIXTL1PU), Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Extended Lifecycle Support (ELS) nodes, and McAfee-integrated Virus Scanning Plug-Ins (2070VSP Series). Form, Fit, and Function: Software must execute native cross-domain security filtering and multi-level desktop access without requiring modification to existing agency security classification boundary policies. B. HARDWARE APPLIANCES AND HARDWARE MAINTENANCE Data Diode Appliances: Fiber-optic hardware-enforced one-way data transfer appliances (FDD10G Series) including annual hardware warranty and associated software maintenance. Cross-Domain Access (CDA) & Verifier Hardware: G2CI Cross Domain Access V2 custom hardware and hardware maintenance (1079H-CDA Series) and High-Speed Verifier turnkey appliances (HSVT Series). Form, Fit, and Function: Hardware units must conform to standard 19-inch rack-mount form factors, interface with existing fiber-optic distribution fabrics, and satisfy DoD physical separation and emissions containment standards. C. SPECIALIZED ENGINEERING AND TECHNICAL SERVICES Direct Tier-3/4 Engineering Support: Dedicated Junior, Mid-level, and Senior Product Engineers (5000/5001/5002-CDA Series) possessing relevant security clearances to provide on-site/remote deployment, complex troubleshooting, and integration. Training and Operational Travel: Basic and advanced CDA system administration training (40003-CDA Series) and associated travel (PS-TRAV-CDA) in support of mission locations. If submitting a quote for brand name equivalents, your quote must be supported by a capability statement (3-page limit, 11 pt. font) and a crosswalk of proposed alternatives to the requirements listed herein. title: EVOS M5000 microscope for monitoring and documenting cultured cell images
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 75N98026Q01227 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for EVOS M5000 Microscope for Monitoring and Documenting Cultured Cell Images. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), intends to procure, on a sole source basis, an EVOS M5000 Imaging System from the manufacturer, Thermo Fisher Scientific. The EVOS M5000 Imaging System is required to support cell imaging and analysis conducted by the laboratory within the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS). The system will be used to image and analyze cells grown in culture and is a critical component of new and ongoing research projects. The EVOS M5000 Imaging System will replace aging and outdated imaging equipment that no longer meets the laboratory's current requirements for work involving cultured cells. The required system provides the specific combination of capabilities necessary for the laboratory's research, including a compact, fully integrated configuration suitable for use within the laboratory's existing biological safety cabinet (BSC); position tracking for longitudinal monitoring of live cells; integrated quantitative analysis for cell counting, confluence, and transfection/transduction efficiency; and multi-modal imaging of both live cultured cells and fixed or fluorescently stained specimens. The Government intends to procure the EVOS M5000 Imaging System on a sole-source basis from Thermo Fisher Scientific. The required system includes a fully integrated digital inverted microscope capable of four-color fluorescence, transmitted-light, and color imaging; a high-sensitivity 3.2 MP monochrome camera; autofocus; Z-stacking; time-lapse imaging; position-sensing X/Y stage and software-based location tracking; and onboard software for cell imaging and quantitative analysis. The system is required to support cell counting, confluence assessment, and determination of transfection/transduction efficiency and shall be capable of imaging live cells and fixed or fluorescently stained cells in culture vessels and on glass microscope slides. The system shall be sufficiently compact and fully integrated to operate within the laboratory's existing biological safety cabinet. The laboratory conducted market research and evaluated commercially available alternatives to avoid unnecessarily restricting this acquisition to a single manufacturer. Three systems were evaluated, including the Thermo Fisher Scientific EVOS M5000 Imaging System, the ECHO Revolve, and the Logos Biosystems CELENA S Digital Imaging System. Manufacturer specifications and system capabilities were reviewed and compared, including physical configuration and footprint, live-cell imaging capabilities, fluorescence and transmitted-light imaging, sample compatibility, cell-analysis functions, and longitudinal imaging capabilities. Although the ECHO Revolve and CELENA S provide several comparable microscopy functions, neither was identified as providing the complete combination of capabilities required by the laboratory. The EVOS M5000 was therefore determined to meet the laboratory's overall technical and operational requirements. Due to the specialized nature of the laboratory's research and the Government's requirement for the specific combination of a fully integrated microscope configuration, BSC compatibility, live-cell imaging, position tracking, quantitative cell-analysis capabilities, and multi-modal imaging, the Government intends to procure the EVOS M5000 Imaging System on a sole-source basis from Thermo Fisher Scientific. Thermo Fisher Scientific manufactures the EVOS M5000 Imaging System and, based on the market research conducted, is the only source identified that can satisfy the Government's complete combination of scientific and technical requirements. Use of an alternate system could require modifications to the laboratory's established imaging workflow and methodologies and could affect the laboratory's ability to conduct longitudinal cell monitoring and consistent quantitative analysis. The contractor shall provide the Thermo Fisher Scientific EVOS M5000 Imaging System in accordance with the requirements of this solicitation. The system shall provide a fully integrated digital inverted microscope capable of four-color fluorescence, transmitted-light, and color imaging; a high-sensitivity 3.2 MP monochrome camera; autofocus; Z-stacking; time-lapse imaging; position-sensing X/Y stage and software-based location tracking; and onboard software for cell imaging and quantitative analysis. The system shall support cell counting, confluence assessment, and determination of transfection/transduction efficiency and shall be capable of imaging live cells and fixed or fluorescently stained cells in culture vessels and on glass microscope slides. The system shall be sufficiently compact and fully integrated to operate within the laboratory's existing biological safety cabinet. The contractor shall deliver the required equipment to NIEHS in Rall Building 101, laboratories E144-146, located at 111 T.W. Alexander Drive, Research Triangle Park, North Carolina 27709. Acceptance will be demonstrated by successful delivery and successful operation of the specified imaging system within the NIEHS laboratory. There is no travel for this purchase. This RFQ is being posted to the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE) in accordance with RFO FAR 5.201. This acquisition will be conducted in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12 � Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, using the simplified procedures at RFO FAR 12.201-1. Required delivery date: September 25, 2026 Delivery Location: NIEHS, Rall Building 101, Laboratories E144-146, 111 T.W. Alexander Drive, Research Triangle Park, NC 27709 The applicable NAICS code is 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. The applicable PSC is 6650 � Optical Instruments, Test Equipment, Components and Accessories. Please see the attached requirements document titled �75N98026Q01227 � Requirements Document� for additional information. 2.0 UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OF THE CONTRACTOR The proposed contractor, Thermo Fisher Scientific, is the manufacturer of the required EVOS M5000 Imaging System for cell imaging and analysis conducted by the laboratory within the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS). The required equipment is a specialized, fully integrated digital inverted microscope designed to provide four-color fluorescence, transmitted-light, and color imaging of cultured cells and fixed or fluorescently stained specimens. The system includes a high-sensitivity 3.2 MP monochrome camera, autofocus, Z-stacking, time-lapse imaging, position tracking, and integrated software for quantitative cell analysis, including cell counting, confluence assessment, and determination of transfection/transduction efficiency. The EVOS M5000 Imaging System is specialized research equipment required to support the Government's established approach for imaging and analyzing cells grown in culture, including live-cell longitudinal monitoring and analysis of fixed or fluorescently stained specimens. The system's compact, fully integrated configuration is required to permit operation within the laboratory's existing biological safety cabinet while providing the imaging, position-tracking, and quantitative analysis capabilities necessary for the laboratory's research. title: FEMA Region 6 Watch Control Room Consoles and Furniture
description: The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Region 6, is issuing a solicitation for the FEMA Region 6 Watch Control Room Consoles and Furniture requirement at the Federal Regional Center located at 800 N. Loop 288, Denton, Texas 76209. The purpose of this requirement is to refresh the Regional Watch Center furniture and provide furniture suitable for 24/7/365 watch center operations. The requirement includes procurement, delivery, assembly, installation, positioning, and configuration of the following: Eight (8) Think Chairs Eight (8) Workstation Chairs Eight (8) Control Console Units One (1) Conference Table Brand-name-or-equal products are permitted. Any proposed equal product must meet or exceed the salient characteristics identified in the SOW and the solicitation. The contractor shall provide all furniture components, hardware, parts, materials, labor, equipment, supervision, and supplies necessary for proper use and full functionality. All products shall be new. Used, reworked, refurbished, or discontinued products are not acceptable. All products shall meet or exceed applicable ANSI/BIFMA performance standards and applicable flame spread/fire rating requirements identified in the solicitation. The contractor shall remove and relocate existing furniture and chairs to the on-campus East Storage Shed in coordination with the Contracting Officer�s Representative. The contractor shall remove all packaging, debris, pallets, wrapping, surplus materials, and waste from the site and shall not use Government waste receptacles or onsite dumpsters. The contractor shall coordinate delivery and installation with the Government. Contractor personnel shall comply with all FEMA facility access, security, conduct, safety, and site-use requirements. Final acceptance will occur after Government inspection confirms all items are installed, functional, and compliant with the solicitation requirements. Vendors shall reference the attached Statement of Work, SOW, for the complete scope of work, technical specifications, delivery, installation, security, and acceptance requirements. The deadline for submission of questions is extended until September 17, 2026. Responses to all questions received will be posted on September 18, 2026. The proposal submission deadline is extended until Monday, September 21, 2026. Submissions shall be emailed to: Barbara Gonzalez Contract Specialist barbara.gonzalez@fema.dhs.gov Neddra Tucker Contracting Officer neddra.tucker@fema.dhs.gov

Requirement: For Supplies: This requirement is for (1) Hydrovac Excavator in accordance with the Statement of Work (SOW). CLIN SUPPLIES QUANTITY UNIT 0001 Hydrovac Excavator 1 EACH 2. Provisions and Clauses: See solicitation attachment for applicable provisions and clauses that apply to this acquisition. NOTE 1: In accordance with R-DFARS 252.204-7998, Alternate A, Annual Representations and Certifications (Deviation 2026-O0043) (FEB 2026), the offeror's quote submission legally binds and certifies that its SAM registration is current, complete, accurate, and has been updated within the preceding 12 months as of the offer's date. NOTE 2: In accordance with R-DFARS 252.204-7021 and R-DFARS 252.204-7025, a CMMC Level 1 assessment is the mandatory minimum requirement for all offerors bidding with the Department of War. Under CMMC Level 1, all offerors must demonstrate full compliance by self-certifying with the 15 basic safeguarding requirements for Federal Contract Information (FCI) outlined in RFO 52.240-93(b)(1). Once your organization has confirmed its compliance with these 15 requirements, you must enter this self-certification into the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) module within PIEE (https://piee.eb.mil). Contract award cannot be made to any offeror that is not fully compliant and whose assessment results are not properly recorded in the system of record. You must verify the CMMC Level required for this award by checking the provisions and clauses within the solicitation. 4. Quotes Due Date: Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Contract Specialist via e-mail at Bryson.pennie@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer at Amanda.hoyng@us.af.mil. Quotes must conform to the requirements of this solicitation and be received no later than 21 Sep 2026 at 12:00 PM EST. It is the responsibility of the offeror to ensure that the quote and its attachments are received. Any correspondence sent via e-mail must contain the subject line �FA860126Q0149 Hydrovac Excavator � The entire quotation must be contained in a single e-mail that does not exceed 5 megabytes including attachments, if any. E-mails with compressed files are not permitted. Note that e-mail filters at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base are designed to filter e-mails without subject lines or with suspicious subject lines or contents (i.e., .exe or .zip files). Therefore, if the specified subject line is not included, the e-mail may not get through the e-mail filters. Also be advised that .zip or .exe files are not allowable attachments and may be deleted by the email filters at Wright-Patterson. If sending attachments with email, ensure only .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls or .xlsx documents are sent. The email filter may delete any other form of attachments. If a DoDSafe drop off is needed, please notify the contract specialist or contracting officer at least 48 hours before quotes are due. Any quotes received after designated closing date and time need not be considered. Quotes must include aggregate total of base plus all option year CLINS, if requested (IAW RFO 52.217-5 Evaluation of Options). All quotes shall be in whole dollars and conform to the Contract Line-Item Number (CLIN) structure of attached solicitation. 5. Notice to Vendor(s): All vendors must fully complete and return the 'Required Information Sheet' (attached to the solicitation) and return with their quotation. Additionally, quotations that contain pricing only with no description/detail of the supply/service that will be provided will not be accepted or considered for award. 6. Tariffs: In accordance with R-DFARS 252.225-7013, the contractor is prohibited from including any amount for customs duties on eligible items within the quote price. The claim for duty-free entry is restricted to supplies destined for government use, either as end items or as components thereof. The Government will provide assistance in the process of obtaining duty-free entry. 7. Period of Acceptance of Quotes: Offeror agrees to hold prices in its quote firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers. 8. SAM Registration: Firms submitting a quote for the solicitation described herein, MUST be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database, or risk the quote as being non-responsive, regardless of the package being considered complete, timely or any other salient consideration. Information to register on SAM can be found at the web site, SAM.gov. List of Attachments: Solicitation Statement of Work

title: USACE History Office (CEHO) Historical Support Services BPA
description: The Office of History, Headquarters, U.S. Corps of Engineers (CEHO), located in Alexandria, Virginia, is responsible for collecting, preserving, interpreting, and disseminating the history of the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE). To accomplish its mission, CEHO's staff of historians, curators, archivists, and editors conducts the following activities: research, write, and review a wide variety of historical products; collect, arrange, catalog, and preserve historical documents, photographs, and artifacts; and conduct a wide-ranging oral history program. To advance it mission, CEHO requires historical services contractors to support CEHO; all USACE organizations and activities; the history and museum staffs at U.S. Army Engineer School at Ft. Leonard Wood, Missouri. The solicitation is to establish a pool of Blanket Purchase Agreement holders that are capable of performing all the required services in the Performance Work Statement for the Master Blanket Purchase Agreement. All proposal must be received no later than 12:00 PM EST on Monday, 21 September 2026. All requests for clarification must be submitted no later than 5:00 PM EST on Monday, 14 September 2026. Questions received after 5:00 PM EST on Monday, 14 September 2026 are not guaranteed to receive a response. Submit all questions and inquiries to the Point of Contract listed in the Solicitation. See the attached Solicitation and attachments for additional information. 9 September 2026 Update: Responses to several questions have been posted - see "Response to KTR Questions" document.

title: COMBINED PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT: 5-year IDIQ/Enterprise Contract for Everfox Software Licenses, Maintenance and Support Services
description: COMBINED PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT (COMMERCIAL OFF-THE-SHELF EVERSOFT SOFTWARE) FAR Part 12 This special notice meets posting requirements of RFO FAR 5.1, 6.1, 12.1 and DFARS 206.3. It also serves as market research pursuant to RFO FAR 10. The Government intends to award a 5-year, sole-source, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)/Enterprise Contract (EC) with the first order to be issued prior to the conclusion of Fiscal Year 2026. Anticipated Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Intended Sole Source OEM: Everfox (https://www.everfox.com/) Estimated Contract Ceiling: $75M-$90M This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIRED SUPPLIES AND SERVICES The Government has an ongoing operational requirement to procure enterprise-level, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software licenses, specialized hardware appliances, hardware/software maintenance, and engineering support services provided by Everfox. (or brand-name equivalent solutions satisfying all salient characteristics) The requirement encompasses a 5-year Ordering Period. Specific part numbers, nomenclature, and projected annual quantities across the total ordering period are itemized in the attached spreadsheet ("Attachment 1 - Requirements Listing"). The required supplies and services are categorized across three core areas: A. SOFTWARE LICENSES, SUBSCRIPTIONS, AND MAINTENANCE Cross-Domain Guards: Perpetual and subscription licenses, standard maintenance, and associated filter bundles for Structured Guard (2070 Series), Unstructured Guard (2068 Series), and High-Speed Guard (2071 Series) supporting multi-network data transfer. Centralized Management & Endpoint Access: Control Center Server and Managed Device subscriptions (CCMDS/CCSVS Series) and Trusted Thin Client (TTC) Distribution Console, End User Device (EUD), and Network Resource licenses (10251 Series). Collaboration & Security Plugins: Everfox Information eXchange (DSIXTL1PU), Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Extended Lifecycle Support (ELS) nodes, and McAfee-integrated Virus Scanning Plug-Ins (2070VSP Series). Form, Fit, and Function: Software must execute native cross-domain security filtering and multi-level desktop access without requiring modification to existing agency security classification boundary policies. B. HARDWARE APPLIANCES AND HARDWARE MAINTENANCE Data Diode Appliances: Fiber-optic hardware-enforced one-way data transfer appliances (FDD10G Series) including annual hardware warranty and associated software maintenance. Cross-Domain Access (CDA) & Verifier Hardware: G2CI Cross Domain Access V2 custom hardware and hardware maintenance (1079H-CDA Series) and High-Speed Verifier turnkey appliances (HSVT Series). Form, Fit, and Function: Hardware units must conform to standard 19-inch rack-mount form factors, interface with existing fiber-optic distribution fabrics, and satisfy DoD physical separation and emissions containment standards. C. SPECIALIZED ENGINEERING AND TECHNICAL SERVICES Direct Tier-3/4 Engineering Support: Dedicated Junior, Mid-level, and Senior Product Engineers (5000/5001/5002-CDA Series) possessing relevant security clearances to provide on-site/remote deployment, complex troubleshooting, and integration. Training and Operational Travel: Basic and advanced CDA system administration training (40003-CDA Series) and associated travel (PS-TRAV-CDA) in support of mission locations. All responsible sources�including OEM-authorized commercial resellers and distributors�may submit a quote for the exact products (or brand-name equivalents) and quantities listed in Attachment 1. If submitting a quote for brand name equivalents, your quote must be supported by a capability statement (3-page limit, 11 pt. font) and a crosswalk of proposed alternatives to the requirements listed herein. Quoted Pricing Submission Requirements: Pricing must be separated by year Each line item must include Part Number, Product Description, PoP, Type, unit pricing and extended pricing Any additional fees Attach the End User License Agreement (EULA)/ End User Service Agreement (EUSA) and include a statement of understanding that the attached addendum (Attachment 2 � Federal SLA Addendum) or one patently similar (and approved by the Contracting Officer after legal review) MUST be signed by the OEM prior to award.

description: 1.0 Combined Synopsis / Solicitation Statement (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(i)) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.202, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Solicitation Identification: Solicitation number 70LGLY26Q00000060 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for the procurement of a Classified Sound-Attenuated Door and Split-Frame Assembly Package for Room 8 at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC), Glynco, GA. Small Business Set-Aside Status: This acquisition is 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS code 561622. PSC: 5670 Provisions and Clauses: This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference and in full text. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR): https://www.acquisition.gov/ Homeland Security Acquisition Regulation (HSAR): https://www.acquisition.gov/hsar Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS): DPAS rating is not assigned to this commercial requirement 2.0 Contract Schedule of Supplies (CLIN Structure) (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(ii)) The Government contemplates the award of a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Commercial Purchase Order resulting from this RFQ. CLIN: 00001 Description: STC 50 Sound-Attenuated Wood Door, Split Frame & Complete Hardware Package Quantity: 1.0 Unit of Issue: LOT Unit Price: Total Firm-Fixed-Price Pricing Terms & Tax Status: All-Inclusive Firm-Fixed-Price: Quoted pricing for CLIN 0001 is all-inclusive. All crating, in-transit insurance, freight transportation (FOB Destination), delivery, and hardware components must be included in the lump-sum price. Tax Exemption: The United States Federal Government is tax-exempt. No state, local, or sales taxes shall be applied. 3.0 Description of Requirement & Salient Characteristics (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(iii)) 3.1 Scope of Requirement This acquisition is strictly for the factory manufacture, hardware integration/preparation, protective crating, and delivery (FOB Destination) of one (1) factory-engineered, high-performance sound-attenuated wood door and split-frame assembly package. The door assembly must achieve an independently certified laboratory sound rating of Sound Transmission Class (STC) 50 or higher to satisfy federal standards for classified and secure discussion spaces (Secure Compartmented Information Facility [SCIF] / Secure Working Area [SWA] standards). Note: This contract is for supply-only delivery. Field installation, on-site wall integration, and perimeter drywall work are excluded. 3.2 Salient Physical, Functional, and Performance Characteristics To be deemed technically acceptable, the quoted door and frame package must meet or exceed all of the following minimum criteria: Door Leaf Construction & Acoustic Rating: Dimensions: Nominal size 3070 (3'-0" Width x 7'-0" Height; approximately 36" W x 84" H). Thickness conforming to manufacturer's certified STC 50 cross-sectional design (1-3/4" to 2-1/2"). Core & Faces: Premium architectural-grade wood veneer faces over an engineered acoustical damping core, resin-bonded to prevent warping, delamination, or acoustical flanking under continuous cycling. Acoustical Performance: Must achieve an independently certified rating of STC 50 minimum when tested in accordance with ASTM E90 and calculated per ASTM E413. Fire Labeling: Where required by facility wall design, permanent certified UL or Warnock Hersey (WHI) positive pressure fire label (minimum 20-minute). Split-Frame Assembly & Sound Sealing System: Frame Style: Heavy-duty acoustically engineered split steel frame (minimum 14-gauge or 16-gauge cold-rolled or galvannealed steel) designed for slip-on retrofit wrapping around finished interior drywall/stud wall assemblies. Jamb Depth: Sized to match the specific finished wall thickness of Room 8. Perimeter Acoustic Seals: Integrated dual/perimeter compression acoustic seals seated into recessed frame stops, maintaining airtight perimeter sound gasketing without causing latch binding. Threshold & Automatic Door Bottom (ADB): Heavy-duty extruded aluminum sound-rated threshold paired with a concealed or semi-mortised automatic mechanical drop-down door bottom seal that seats firmly upon closing and retracts upon opening. Hardware Suite & Factory Preparations (Brand Name or Equal): Locking Mechanism & Cylinder: Commercial heavy-duty mortise lockset factory-installed into the leaf, configured to receive a Schlage Model 20-079 626 satin chrome 6-pin/7-pin key cylinder (or technical equivalent fully compatible with FLETC key management). Hinges: Heavy-duty, precision-machined cam-lift hinges engineered for high-mass acoustic leaves. Hinges must slightly elevate the door upon opening to clear the threshold seal and seat firmly against perimeter seals when closed. Door Closer: Heavy-duty, surface-mounted commercial door closer conforming to LCN 4040XP in aluminum powder coat finish (or approved equal), featuring adjustable spring sizes 1�6, hydraulic backcheck, and delayed action to overcome acoustic seal resistance. Internal Wiring Raceway: Factory-drilled continuous internal conduit raceway within the door core to allow future wiring of access control hardware without violating acoustic integrity. Electronic Power Transfer (EPT): Precision factory mortise prep on door edge and frame jamb for an architectural EPT unit (e.g., Securitron EPT, Von Duprin EPT-10, or approved equivalent), with the physical EPT device prepped and shipped loose. General Quality & Warranty: New Equipment Only: All items must be newly manufactured, unused, and in pristine condition (no surplus or remanufactured goods). Commercial Warranty: Standard commercial warranty (minimum one year) covering defects, structural core integrity, acoustic seal durability, and mechanical hardware. 4.0 Delivery, Inspection, and Acceptance (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(iv)) Delivery Schedule: Delivery shall be completed within 60 calendar days After Receipt of Order (ARO). F.O.B. Terms: F.O.B. Destination only. The contractor is responsible for freight charges, transit insurance, offloading at the receiving dock, and safe transit. Delivery & Acceptance Location: Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) 1131 Chapel Crossing Road, Building 261 Receiving Glynco, GA 31524 Attn: Room 8 Project / Physical Security Office Packaging & Protective Crating: The door leaf and split frame must be enclosed in heavy-duty wooden shipping crates or pallet enclosures with internal corner edge protection, moisture-barrier wrapping, and transit shock indicators. Loose hardware must be segregated and clearly labeled in internal sub-boxes. Inspection & Acceptance: Destination inspection and final acceptance will be conducted by FLETC Physical Security and Receiving personnel upon verification of certified laboratory STC 50 test reports, rough opening compatibility, and complete hardware bill of materials. 5.0 Section L, Addendum to FAR 52.212-1: Submission Instructions Offerors shall submit complete electronic quotation packages to Contracting Officer Ricardo Soto via email prior to the closing deadline. Quotations must include the following separate parts: Part I � Technical Capability & Delivery Schedule (Non-Price): Standard Form 1449 / Amendment Acknowledgments: Completed and signed SF-1449 (Blocks 17a, 30a, 30b, 30c) and any issued SF-30 amendments. Certified Acoustic Laboratory Test Report: Independent laboratory sound test report (in strict accordance with ASTM E90 and ASTM E413) validating an STC 50 minimum rating for the quoted door slab, frame profile, and perimeter seal assembly.
