title: Request for Information (RFI) Obtaining Food Franchise Rights in Washington, DC - Northern Capital Region (NCR)
description: Request for Information (RFI) : Obtaining Food Franchise Rights in Washington, DC - Northern Capital Region (NCR) The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to gather detailed input from qualified organizations regarding the requirements, processes, and opportunities associated with obtaining food franchise rights within the Northern Capital Region (NCR), Washington, DC. Organizations responding to this RFI are requested to provide all relevant documentation, points of contact, marketing materials, and procedural information. This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only and does not obligate the Government to pursue any further action or future solicitation. Direct Engagement Model � Industry Feedback Requested In addition to information on obtaining food franchise rights generally, the FBI is specifically interested in understanding the feasibility and attractiveness of a direct-engagement model, in which the FBI would contract or otherwise arrange directly with individual food franchise brands (rather than through a single master food-service contractor) to provide food service operations within the J. Edgar Hoover Building (JEH), Washington, DC. What the FBI should understand about this model: Typical franchise agreement structures, term lengths, and capital investment requirements (buildout, equipment, branding) when a franchisor/franchisee operates within a federal government-controlled facility rather than a traditional commercial or retail location Licensing, royalty, and territory considerations that may apply or require modification for a single-tenant government building Food safety, supply chain, and operational standards the franchise would need to meet or adapt to operate within a secure federal facility Any precedent for franchise operations within federal buildings, military installations, or other access-controlled environments, and lessons learned from those arrangements All responses must be submitted to: Ms. McKenzie P. Bucher, mpbucher@fbi.gov Mr. Tom Teets, twteets@fbi.gov Please provide all requested information no later than September 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM EDT.

title: Academic Standards, Curricular Alignment, and Professional Learning Support Services
description: This Notice of Intent is prepared in accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2, Synopsis of Proposed Contract Actions for the Academic Standards, Curricular Alignment, and Professional Learning Support Services Requirement. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. A SOLICITATION WILL NOT BE POSTED. The Government intends to award a sole-source service contract to the incumbent contractor in support of the Department of War Education Activity's (DoWEA) ongoing Do No Harm initiative. The contractor previously conducted an independent third-party audit of curriculum, professional development, school discipline, counseling services, special education programs, academic standards, and related policies. The proposed acquisition will support DoWEA's enterprise-wide implementation of audit findings and recommendations and includes development of integrated action plans, standards alignment, policy development, stakeholder engagement, performance assessments, implementation support, and related services necessary to execute the follow-on effort. title: Amendment 1 (Clarifications Q&A) to: Army Blood Link (ABL) � Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS)
description: Army Blood Link (ABL) � Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) for Blood Product Transport Request for Proposals (RFP) � Other Transaction Authority (OTA) Prototype Project This amendment provides clarifications in response to vendor questions and addresses identified information gaps. Please refer to the attachment titled �Amendment 1� for the complete list of questions and answers. For any additional clarification, please contact the points of contact listed in this notice. Brief Description of Requirement The 419th Contracting Support Brigade, Fort Liberty, North Carolina, on behalf of XVIII Airborne Corps Joint Operations Innovation Outpost (JIOP), is issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) for the competitive award of an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) prototype project for the Army Blood Link (ABL) Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS). The Government seeks to develop and deliver two (2) prototype UAS capable of transporting 20 units of Government?designated blood products per mission, including all approved primary, secondary, thermal?control, shock?protection, monitoring, and restraint packaging. Each system shall provide a minimum usable payload?compartment volume of 1.25 cubic feet and a minimum payload capacity of 35 pounds, with a payload capacity range of 25�50 pounds. The contractor shall provide a validated transport container that maintains the Government?specified product temperature range for the required mission duration and environmental conditions. The ABL UAS will be employed in contested and denied environments where ground transportation is not viable and will support both training and deployed operational missions for medical units (e.g., medical brigades). Additional technical, performance, and interface requirements are provided in the attached Salient Characteristics � Army Blood Link (ABL) UAS for Blood Product Transport, which form an integral part of this notice and the basis for proposal evaluation. Period and Place of Performance a. Prototype Period of Performance (PoP): The anticipated PoP for the prototype OTA is up to 3 months from effective date of award, unless otherwise negotiated. (Recommend modification of existing commercial UAS) Offerors shall propose a schedule that delivers fully functional prototype systems (including complete payload containers and support equipment) no later than 3 months after award, including time allocated to testing, refinement, and documentation in coordination with the Government. b. Place of Performance / Delivery Location: Primary delivery and demonstration locations will be within the continental United States (CONUS). The initial delivery location is anticipated to be: Fort Liberty, North Carolina (or other designated XVIII Airborne Corps / medical unit location). Specific delivery instructions, test locations, and access requirements will be provided at time of award and coordinated with the Agreements Officer�s Representative (AOR). Anticipated Agreement Information a. Type of Instrument: This effort will be executed as a prototype project agreement under DoD Other Transaction Authority (OTA). b. Type of Contract/Agreement Consideration: The ABL prototype effort will be structured as a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) OTA agreement for the design, integration, delivery, and demonstration of the prototype systems, in accordance with the DoD OTA Guide and applicable implementing guidance. c. Acquisition Procedures: Acquisition procedures will follow OTA prototype project procedures as outlined in the DoD OTA Guide and implementing Army guidance for competitive prototype projects. d. Authority: This prototype project is pursued under Title 10, U.S.C., Section 4022 (Other Transaction Authority for Prototype Projects). e. Follow?On Production: This competitive prototype project may result in a follow?on production agreement (which may be FFP or other appropriate structure) without the use of competitive procedures, consistent with Title 10, U.S.C., Section 4022. Follow?on production is contingent upon: Successful completion of the prototype effort, as determined by the AOR; and Increased or continued demand for the ABL capability; and A clear Government determination that a follow?on production award is in the best interest of the Government. Summary of Technical and Operational Requirements The ABL UAS shall meet or exceed the requirements set forth in the attached Salient Characteristics document, including but not limited to: Mission Role & Employment: Transport Government?designated blood products in contested/denied environments where ground transportation is not viable. Support training missions (1�5 per month) and operational deployments (multiple missions per day). Payload Capacity & Volume: Transport 20 blood units including all packaging and protection. Minimum usable payload volume 1.25 ft�. Payload capacity range 25�50 lb, with minimum 35 lb capability. Blood Transport Container & Thermal Control: Validated container compatible with UAS payload bay. Maintain required blood temperature for up to 3 hours at 15 �F to 120 �F with high humidity. Protection against rain, dust, sand, solar heating, and chemical contamination. Range, Endurance & Mission Distance: Minimum 30 km one?way operational radius at maximum combined fuel/energy and payload load. 100 km maximum mission distance (total route). 3�6 hours of operating time per mission, while ensuring blood remains within specified temperature limits (? 3 hours in container). Operations & Environment: Day and night operations. Operation from ground level to 18,000 ft. Operate at 15 �F to 120 �F, high humidity. Delivery & Accuracy: Delivery?location accuracy of ? 10 meters. Support ground/landing delivery and optional aerial drop from 10�15 m without compromising blood integrity. Command, Control & Communications: Minimum 30?mile communications range between aircraft and ground control station. Single?operator control of at least one aircraft, with architecture that allows multiple aircraft to operate simultaneously in the same area. Autonomy & Detect?and?Avoid: Semi?autonomous flight, waypoint navigation, and return?to?base. Sensors and logic to detect and avoid aircraft and obstacles, suitable for contested/denied environments. Training & Human Factors: Operator training program (approximately 1�3 days) for basic operations, servicing, and field?level repair. System suitable for operation and servicing by typical medical brigade personnel with minimal technical background. Maintainability, Reliability & Service Life: Expected operational life 500�1500 flight hours. Servicing intervals every 300�500 cycles. Field?repairable by unit personnel with modular/line?replaceable components. Minimum 90% probability of successful delivery per mission. At least one?year warranty and obsolescence/parts?availability plan. Regulatory, Origin & Approval Requirements: Design and documentation sufficient to support U.S. Army Systems Readiness Directorate (SRD) flight approval. No prohibited foreign?made components, foreign software, foreign cloud services, or foreign technical support. Compliance with applicable U.S. and DoD sourcing restrictions. Meeting these salient characteristics within a 20% deviation from the stated parameters is acceptable; however, proposals will be evaluated competitively and only one awardee is anticipated. title: Gas Chromatograph with a Thermal Conductivity Detector and Flame Ioniztion Detector with Methanizer
description: ***Amendment 0001**** Amendment 0001 provides resposnes to questions received in response to the solicitation. Q.1. I am reviewing Notice ID 1333ND26QNB640601 and would appreciate some clarification regarding the analytical requirements. Would you be able to share the analytes of interest, the required detection limits, and the expected concentration ranges for the system? A.1. This analyzer will be used for the analysis of binary gas mixtures in nitrogen or air balance gases. The analyses performed will include a wide range of gaseous standard reference materials including: 1 ppm methane in air and 250 ppm carbon monoxide in nitrogen, both analyzed using the flame ionization detector with methanation, and 0.5 % carbon dioxide in nitrogen analyzed using the thermal conductivity detector. This analyzer will also be used for analyses of ambient level CO in air mixtures, ranging from (40 � 200) ppb. Q.2. What types of samples will be tested? A.2. This analyzer will be used for analyses of high pressure gas mixtures in nitrogen or air balance gases. Q.3. What specific substances or compounds need to be detected or analyzed in these samples? If available, please also share any specific testing standards or requirements. With this information, we can better understand your application and recommend a suitable instrument configuration and quotation accordingly. A.3. As stated above, this analyzer will be used for the analysis of high pressure gas mixtures delivered at or below 25 psig. The analyses performed will include a wide range of gaseous standard reference materials including: 1 ppm methane in air and 250 ppm carbon monoxide in nitrogen, both analyzed using the flame ionization detector with methanation, and 0.5 % carbon dioxide in nitrogen analyzed using the thermal conductivity detector. For improved precision, temperature ramping and stable detector response are required to achieve baseline resolution between components in air balance gas. In all cases the repeatability should be at or below 0.2 % relative area counts. Q.4. Regarding your software requirements, you cite Visual Basic Version 6.0. Would that software be able to generate an XML file to communicate with our software (CompassCDS)? A.4. The visual basic software was developed to support communication between the GC software and a 12-port dead-end VICI sampling valve. The software can retrieve data from a txt file generated by the GC software and output the data to excel. There is not an extension to the solicitation as a result of this amendment. The question period for this soliciation will close today, September 17,2026, at 4:00 PM ET. End of Amendment 0001 ******** See attached.

description: The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Region 6, is issuing a solicitation for the FEMA Region 6 Watch Control Room Consoles and Furniture requirement at the Federal Regional Center located at 800 N. title: Promega Assay Reagents to Support Complement-ARIE Mechanistic Toxicology Research
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 75N98026Q01226 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Promega assay reagents to support Complement-ARIE mechanistic toxicology research. The Government intends to award a purchase order on a sole-source basis to Promega Corporation based on the Government's determination that Promega Corporation is the only source identified as capable of satisfying the Government's requirements. However, all responsible sources may submit a quotation that demonstrates their ability to satisfy the complete requirements identified in this RFQ and the attached requirements document. All timely quotations will be considered by the Government. This RFQ is being posted to the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE) in accordance with RFO FAR 5.201. This acquisition will be conducted in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12 � Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, using the simplified procedures at RFO FAR 12.201-1. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), intends to procure, on a sole source basis, Promega assay reagents from the manufacturer, Promega Corporation, 2800 Woods Hollow Road, Madison, Wisconsin 53711. The Promega assay reagents are required to support Complement-ARIE research conducted by the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) and NIEHS through the Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT). The reagents will be used to assess cell viability, liver injury, liver function, oxidative stress, antioxidant responses, and cellular bioenergetics in human three-dimensional microphysiological systems and will complement cell painting and omics endpoints. Continued use of the specified assay reagents is necessary to support the established experimental approach, maintain consistency and comparability of research results, and provide the required sensitivity for evaluating toxicity responses in small three-dimensional microtissue models. Due to the specialized nature of the Complement-ARIE research and the Government�s requirement for the specific combination of assay reagents, luminescence/chemiluminescence-based detection, toxicological endpoints, and compatibility with the established experimental approach, the Government intends to procure these supplies on a sole-source basis from Promega Corporation. Promega Corporation manufactures the assay reagents identified in the Government�s requirement and, based on the market research conducted, is the only source identified that can satisfy the Government�s requirements. The Government has determined that these requirements are necessary to support the established research methodology, maintain comparability and reproducibility of results, and enable integration of the assay results with existing cell painting and omics-based analyses. The contractor shall provide the Promega assay reagents identified in the Government�s requirement and associated quotation. The reagents shall support measurement of cell viability, liver injury, liver function, oxidative stress, antioxidant responses, and cellular bioenergetics in human three-dimensional microphysiological systems. The contractor shall deliver the required supplies to NIEHS in Rall Building 101, laboratories E144-146, located at 111 T.W. Alexander Drive, Research Triangle Park, North Carolina 27709. Acceptance will be demonstrated by successful delivery and the successful performance of the specified assays within the NIEHS laboratory. There is no travel for this purchase. Required delivery date: September 25, 2026 Delivery Location: NIEHS, Rall Building 101, Laboratories E144-146, 111 T.W. Alexander Drive, Research Triangle Park, NC 27709 The applicable NAICS code is 325413 � In-Vitro Diagnostic Substance Manufacturing. The applicable PSC is 6550 � In Vitro Diagnostic Substances, Reagents, Test Kits and Sets. Please see the attached requirements document titled �75N98026Q01226 � Requirements Document� for additional information. 2.0 UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OF THE CONTRACTOR The proposed contractor, Promega Corporation, is the manufacturer of the required assay reagents for the Complement-ARIE research conducted by NCATS and NIEHS. The required supplies involve specialized assay reagents designed to measure cell viability, liver injury, liver function, oxidative stress, antioxidant responses, and cellular bioenergetics in human three-dimensional microphysiological systems. The requested reagents also provide luminescence/chemiluminescence-based detection and are intended to complement established cell-painting and omics-based endpoints. The Promega assay reagents are specialized research products that are required to support the Government�s established experimental approach for evaluating toxicity-induced liver injury and associated cellular responses in human three-dimensional microphysiological systems. Due to the specific combination of required toxicological endpoints, detection technology, and compatibility with the established Complement-ARIE research methodology, use of an alternate source could require modifications to the experimental design and methodologies, affect assay sensitivity, and reduce the comparability and reproducibility of results across the research program. Accordingly, Promega Corporation is the only identified responsible source capable of providing the complete combination of assay reagents required to meet the Government�s scientific and technical requirements while maintaining the established experimental approach. BASIS FOR AWARD The Government intends to issue a firm-fixed-price purchase order to Promega Corporation. However, all timely quotations received will be considered. To be considered for award, a quotation must demonstrate that the products offered satisfy all the Government's scientific and technical requirements identified in this RFQ and the attached requirements document. Award will be made to the responsible quoter whose quotation satisfies the Government's requirements and whose price is determined fair and reasonable. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS The response and any other information furnished must be in writing and must contain material in sufficient detail to allow the Office of Acquisition and Logistics Management (OALM) to determine whether the respondent can fulfill the requirement. Quotations shall identify the products being offered, manufacturer and part numbers, quantities, unit and total prices, delivery schedule, and sufficient technical information to demonstrate that the products offered satisfy all of the Government's scientific and technical requirements identified in the attached requirements document. All responses must be sent via email to Contract Specialist, Jordan Neal, at Jordan.Neal@nih.gov, copying Contracting Officer, Alice Pag�n Pereira, at Alice.Pagan@nih.gov by no later than 12:00 pm Eastern Time on Monday, September 21, 2026. To be eligible for award, the contractor must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM.gov) in accordance with applicable requirements. Reference: 75N98026Q01226 on all correspondence.

title: ScriptPro Upgrade and Maintenance
description: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Indian Health Service (HIS) has a need for ScriptPro maintenance and support. The Pharmacy Department utilizes ScriptPro pharmacy automation equipment to support high-volume prescription fulfillment and patient safety. The department fills out approximately 1,000 prescriptions daily. Continued vendor maintenance is required to preserve equipment warranties, reduce medication errors, and ensure accurate National Drug Code (NDC) verification. This requirement combines ongoing maintenance services with a comprehensive operating system and infrastructure upgrade to ensure system reliability, cybersecurity compliance, and continuity of pharmacy operations.

description: The proposed research aims to generate experimental data relevant to battery energy storage system (BESS) usage in rail equipment and use it to validate a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model for assessing explosion hazards in rail applications.

title: Intent to Sole Source - a Preventative Maintenance Agreement (PMA) for the Alpha Omega Machine
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: Alpha Omega. Acquisition Description: The Department of Perioperative Medicine and Dr. Zaghloul is requesting a Preventative Maintenance Agreement (PMA) for the Alpha Omega Machine which is a micro-electrode recording and stimulation system for deep brain stimulation surgery. The purpose of this purchase is to provide the Surgical Neurology Branch with equipment support for a multi-modality micro-electrode recording system that can capture single-unit spiking data, local field potential data, simultaneous surface EEG data, and that can provide real-time online analyses and triggered and patterned electrical stimulation. The PMA for this piece of equipment supports protocol 11-N-0211. The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 253(c) (1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. All responsible sources that could provide the required may submit a capability statement that will be considered by email (subject line to reference NOI-CC-OLAO-26-010000) by 12:00 PM eastern standard time on 09/21/2026 to: valerie.gregorio@nih.gov. All responses received by the closing date of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: The Office of History, Headquarters, U.S. Corps of Engineers (CEHO), located in Alexandria, Virginia, is responsible for collecting, preserving, interpreting, and disseminating the history of the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE). To accomplish its mission, CEHO's staff of historians, curators, archivists, and editors conducts the following activities: research, write, and review a wide variety of historical products; collect, arrange, catalog, and preserve historical documents, photographs, and artifacts; and conduct a wide-ranging oral history program. Field installation, on-site wall integration, and perimeter drywall work are excluded. 3.2 Salient Physical, Functional, and Performance Characteristics To be deemed technically acceptable, the quoted door and frame package must meet or exceed all of the following minimum criteria: Door Leaf Construction & Acoustic Rating: Dimensions: Nominal size 3070 (3'-0" Width x 7'-0" Height; approximately 36" W x 84" H). Thickness conforming to manufacturer's certified STC 50 cross-sectional design (1-3/4" to 2-1/2"). Core & Faces: Premium architectural-grade wood veneer faces over an engineered acoustical damping core, resin-bonded to prevent warping, delamination, or acoustical flanking under continuous cycling. Acoustical Performance: Must achieve an independently certified rating of STC 50 minimum when tested in accordance with ASTM E90 and calculated per ASTM E413. Fire Labeling: Where required by facility wall design, permanent certified UL or Warnock Hersey (WHI) positive pressure fire label (minimum 20-minute). Split-Frame Assembly & Sound Sealing System: Frame Style: Heavy-duty acoustically engineered split steel frame (minimum 14-gauge or 16-gauge cold-rolled or galvannealed steel) designed for slip-on retrofit wrapping around finished interior drywall/stud wall assemblies. Jamb Depth: Sized to match the specific finished wall thickness of Room 8. Perimeter Acoustic Seals: Integrated dual/perimeter compression acoustic seals seated into recessed frame stops, maintaining airtight perimeter sound gasketing without causing latch binding. Threshold & Automatic Door Bottom (ADB): Heavy-duty extruded aluminum sound-rated threshold paired with a concealed or semi-mortised automatic mechanical drop-down door bottom seal that seats firmly upon closing and retracts upon opening. Hardware Suite & Factory Preparations (Brand Name or Equal): Locking Mechanism & Cylinder: Commercial heavy-duty mortise lockset factory-installed into the leaf, configured to receive a Schlage Model 20-079 626 satin chrome 6-pin/7-pin key cylinder (or technical equivalent fully compatible with FLETC key management). Hinges: Heavy-duty, precision-machined cam-lift hinges engineered for high-mass acoustic leaves. Hinges must slightly elevate the door upon opening to clear the threshold seal and seat firmly against perimeter seals when closed. Door Closer: Heavy-duty, surface-mounted commercial door closer conforming to LCN 4040XP in aluminum powder coat finish (or approved equal), featuring adjustable spring sizes 1�6, hydraulic backcheck, and delayed action to overcome acoustic seal resistance. Internal Wiring Raceway: Factory-drilled continuous internal conduit raceway within the door core to allow future wiring of access control hardware without violating acoustic integrity. Electronic Power Transfer (EPT): Precision factory mortise prep on door edge and frame jamb for an architectural EPT unit (e.g., Securitron EPT, Von Duprin EPT-10, or approved equivalent), with the physical EPT device prepped and shipped loose. General Quality & Warranty: New Equipment Only: All items must be newly manufactured, unused, and in pristine condition (no surplus or remanufactured goods). Commercial Warranty: Standard commercial warranty (minimum one year) covering defects, structural core integrity, acoustic seal durability, and mechanical hardware. 4.0 Delivery, Inspection, and Acceptance (FAR 12.202(b)(1)(iv)) Delivery Schedule: Delivery shall be completed within 60 calendar days After Receipt of Order (ARO). F.O.B. Terms: F.O.B. Destination only. The contractor is responsible for freight charges, transit insurance, offloading at the receiving dock, and safe transit. Delivery & Acceptance Location: Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) 1131 Chapel Crossing Road, Building 261 Receiving Glynco, GA 31524 Attn: Room 8 Project / Physical Security Office Packaging & Protective Crating: The door leaf and split frame must be enclosed in heavy-duty wooden shipping crates or pallet enclosures with internal corner edge protection, moisture-barrier wrapping, and transit shock indicators. Loose hardware must be segregated and clearly labeled in internal sub-boxes. Inspection & Acceptance: Destination inspection and final acceptance will be conducted by FLETC P

title: Notice of Intent - Sole Source - SOG Assessment
description: Notice of Intent to award a sole source requirement for SOG Assessment Services to Horizon Performance LLC (UEI: K4U8LGLJ2LG1). This proposed contract action is for SOG Assessment Services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO FAR 13-106-1(b)(1)(i) � Only One Responsible Source. Horizon Performance has successfully implemented a turnkey solution for the BORTAC Selection and Certification Course holistic personnel assessment system. The system is fully operationally capable and currently supports BORTAC�s assessment requirements. BORTAC now requires annual software licensing, continued maintenance, technical consultation, and additional configuration or expansion of capability as required under the period of performance. Horizon Performance is the only source reasonably available to meet this requirement because Horizon Performance developed and currently maintains the customized assessment platform and associated configurations used for the BORTAC Selection and Certification Course. The existing system includes proprietary software, course-specific configurations, assessment structures, reporting tools, and methodology developed for BORTAC�s operational and training environment. Continued annual licensing, maintenance, updates, and technical consultation require access to Horizon Performance�s proprietary software and configuration environment. Due to the complexity and depth of the assessment system, and the requirement to maintain operational continuity, the provider must be able to: Leverage the existing assessment system currently in use and rapidly integrate BORTAC and BORSTAR values, training concepts, operational concepts, and individual performance attributes within the required period of performance. Provide a holistic personnel assessment system based on sound Industrial/Organizational Psychology-backed science, individual high-performance modeling, and a proven application process. Provide qualified Industrial/Organizational Psychology and subject matter expert consulting applicable to the assessment of individuals as part of an elite organization. Provide a developed Commercial Off-The-Shelf customizable software solution with technical configurations specific to the identified SOG training ecosystems. Maintain, update, and modify the existing proprietary system without disruption to the current BORTAC assessment capability. Integrate BORSTAR requirements into the same assessment framework to ensure compatibility of methodology, data structure, reporting, and longitudinal analysis across SOG programs. A change to another vendor would require development of a new assessment system, recreation of BORTAC-specific configurations, potential re-baselining of assessment data, additional validation and consulting support, and transition activities. These activities would result in duplicative cost and delay and would not meet the Government�s requirement for continuity of the existing assessment capability during the required period of performance. BORSTAR�s initial build must be integrated into the existing SOG assessment framework to maintain consistency of methodology, reporting, data structure, and performance analysis across BORTAC and BORSTAR programs. Horizon Performance is the only vendor with the ability to license, maintain, modify, and expand the existing proprietary system to support both BORTAC sustainment and BORSTAR integration within the required timeframe. Market research did not identify another source with the legal rights or technical ability to license, maintain, modify, or expand the existing Horizon Performance system. Therefore, only Horizon Performance is reasonably available for this requirement under FAR 13.106-1(b)(1).
